slides.text: In the marble city of Oakhaven, the Crown levied no taxes in copper or gold. When the treasury ran dry, the King’s Taxidermists walked the cobbles with velvet-lined brass calipers and obsidian needles, harvesting memories from the citizenry. A minor debt cost the taste of summer peaches; a mortgage claimed the face of one’s maternal grandfather. The memories were liquefied into violet ink and cataloged in the grand royal archives, never to be felt again.

Master Silas, the city’s oldest cartographer, sat at his drafting desk when the Taxidermist knocked with an overdue levy from his wife’s final illness. The officer consulted his parchment. 'Only a Tier-One recollection will balance the ledger, old man,' he said coldly, uncapping the crystal vial. Silas had only two Tier-One memories left: the morning his daughter learned to walk along the harbor dock, or the evening twenty years later when her ship vanished beneath the northern ice.

The Taxidermist leaned forward, needle poised at Silas’s temple. 'Choose. Relinquish the joy, or surrender the grief.' Silas closed his rheumy eyes, feeling the warm phantom of his daughter’s tiny hand gripping his thumb, and then the bitter saltwater of her loss. He smiled, pointing to the scar behind his ear where the needle must enter. 'Take her death,' Silas whispered softly. 'Let me live out my remaining winter believing she is still on her way home.'
